symptom: PC1 cannot communicate with PC2
topology_note: Both PCs should belong to VLAN 10 on Switch1.
show_outputs: show vlan brief: Fa0/2 VLAN10; Fa0/3 VLAN20
expected_fault: PC2 access port is assigned to the wrong VLAN

symptom: PC1 cannot reach the VLAN20 gateway
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick is configured between Router1 and Switch1.
show_outputs: show ip interface brief: G0/0.20 192.168.20.1 administratively down
expected_fault: VLAN20 router subinterface is shut down

symptom: PC2 receives an IP but cannot ping its gateway
topology_note: PC2 is configured for VLAN20.
expected_fault: Host has the wrong default gateway

symptom: PC3 cannot communicate with the server in another VLAN
topology_note: Server is connected to VLAN30.
show_outputs: show running-config: interface G0/0.30; encapsulation dot1Q 20
expected_fault: Router subinterface has the wrong VLAN encapsulation ID

symptom: VLAN20 traffic disappears between two switches
topology_note: Switch1 and Switch2 are connected through Gi0/1.
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk: Gi0/1 trunking; allowed VLANs 10,30
expected_fault: VLAN20 is missing from the trunk allowed list

symptom: A newly configured VLAN does not appear on the switch
topology_note: VLAN50 should be used by the lab PCs.
show_outputs: show vlan brief: VLANs 10,20,30,40; VLAN50 absent
expected_fault: Required VLAN was never created

symptom: PC4 loses connectivity after changing its switch port
topology_note: PC4 should use an access port in VLAN10.
show_outputs: show running-config interface Fa0/7: switchport mode trunk
expected_fault: PC access port was incorrectly configured as a trunk

symptom: PC5 cannot access the network
topology_note: PC5 is connected to Switch1 Fa0/8.
show_outputs: show interfaces status: Fa0/8 disabled
expected_fault: PC5's switch interface is administratively disabled

symptom: PC6 cannot communicate after connecting to a new switch
topology_note: The new switch connects to the existing LAN.
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk: no trunk ports displayed
expected_fault: Inter-switch link is operating as an access port instead of a trunk

symptom: PC7 receives an address but cannot contact the DHCP gateway
topology_note: DHCP is configured on Router1 for VLAN20.
show_outputs: show ip dhcp pool: Default gateway 192.168.30.1
expected_fault: DHCP pool specifies an incorrect default-router address

symptom: PC8 automatically receives a 169.254.x.x address
topology_note: PC8 belongs to VLAN30 and uses centralized DHCP.
show_outputs: show running-config interface G0/0.30: no ip helper-address
expected_fault: DHCP relay configuration is missing

symptom: Only VLAN10 clients receive DHCP addresses
topology_note: Router provides DHCP pools for VLAN10 and VLAN20.
show_outputs: show ip dhcp pool: VLAN20 pool missing
expected_fault: DHCP pool for VLAN20 has not been configured

symptom: DHCP server is reachable but clients still receive no address
topology_note: DHCP server is located on another subnet.
show_outputs: show running-config interface G0/0.40: ip helper-address 192.168.10.20
expected_fault: ip helper-address points to an incorrect DHCP server address

symptom: Some DHCP clients receive addresses outside the intended range
topology_note: VLAN10 uses addresses from 192.168.10.0/24.
show_outputs: show ip dhcp binding: 192.168.10.1 assigned to a client
expected_fault: Router gateway address was not excluded from the DHCP pool

symptom: PC9 can ping the DNS server but cannot resolve names
topology_note: DNS server is connected to VLAN30.
show_outputs: nslookup: DNS server timeout
expected_fault: PC is configured with an incorrect DNS server address

symptom: Users can access websites by IP but not by domain name
topology_note: Internet connectivity through the router is working.
show_outputs: ipconfig /all: DNS Server 192.168.50.50; actual DNS server 192.168.30.5
expected_fault: Incorrect DNS server address configured on the client

symptom: Router cannot reach a remote LAN
topology_note: R1 connects to R2 through a serial link.
show_outputs: show ip route: 192.168.40.0/24 not found
expected_fault: Static route to the remote LAN is missing

symptom: Remote users can reach HQ but HQ cannot reach remote users
topology_note: Two routers use manually configured static routes.
show_outputs: R2 routing table contains 192.168.10.0/24; R1 has no route to 192.168.40.0/24
expected_fault: Return route is missing on the HQ router

symptom: OSPF adjacency does not form between two routers
topology_note: R1 and R2 share the 10.0.0.0/30 network.
show_outputs: show ip ospf neighbor: empty; show ip protocols: OSPF not enabled
expected_fault: OSPF is not enabled on the connected interface/network

symptom: OSPF neighbor remains in an incorrect state
topology_note: R1 and R2 should form an adjacency.
show_outputs: show ip ospf interface: R1 hello 10 sec; R2 hello 30 sec
expected_fault: OSPF hello and dead timers do not match

symptom: PC10 can ping the server but cannot use HTTPS
topology_note: An ACL protects the server VLAN.
show_outputs: show access-lists: deny tcp any host 192.168.30.10 eq 443
expected_fault: ACL blocks HTTPS traffic to the server

symptom: Management PC cannot remotely access the router
topology_note: SSH is required for device administration.
show_outputs: show access-lists: deny tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 22
expected_fault: ACL blocks SSH traffic

symptom: Guest VLAN can access the internal database server
topology_note: Guest users should have Internet-only access.
expected_fault: ACL incorrectly permits guest-to-server traffic

symptom: ICMP from the monitoring PC to a router interface fails
topology_note: Monitoring traffic should be allowed through the ACL.
show_outputs: show access-lists: deny icmp host 192.168.10.50 any
expected_fault: ACL blocks ICMP monitoring traffic

symptom: Internal PCs cannot access the Internet after NAT configuration
topology_note: LAN uses 192.168.10.0/24 and connects to an ISP router.
show_outputs: show ip nat translations: empty; show running-config: ip nat inside configured on both interfaces
expected_fault: NAT inside/outside roles are incorrectly configured

symptom: Internet access works for one subnet but not another
topology_note: Router performs PAT for multiple VLANs.
expected_fault: NAT ACL does not include VLAN20

symptom: Wireless clients connect to the SSID but cannot obtain an IP address
topology_note: Access point connects to VLAN40.
show_outputs: show vlan brief: AP switch port in VLAN1; wireless network uses VLAN40
expected_fault: Access point is connected to the wrong VLAN

symptom: Wireless users can connect but cannot reach the gateway
topology_note: SSID is configured for the student network.
show_outputs: show running-config interface Fa0/18: switchport access vlan 10; SSID mapped to VLAN40
expected_fault: AP switch port is assigned to the wrong access VLAN

symptom: Guest wireless users can access each other despite isolation policy
topology_note: Guest clients should be isolated from one another.
show_outputs: AP configuration: client isolation disabled
expected_fault: Wireless client isolation is disabled

symptom: Wireless clients receive addresses but cannot access the Internet
topology_note: Guest wireless network uses VLAN50 and the router provides Internet access.
show_outputs: show ip route: 192.168.50.0/24 connected; no 0.0.0.0/0 route
expected_fault: Default route to the ISP is missing
